predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: Touraine, given in apanage to Philip the Bold in 1360

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Touraine, merged into the crown on 21 October 1422

ledger.x: 1360: the king's son Philip the Bold is created Duke of Touraine: 'He was created Duke of Touraine in 1360'.
1363: Philip the Bold gives Touraine back to the crown: 'in 1363, he returned this duchy to the crown' to receive instead the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage.
1386: the king's brother Louis of Orleans becomes Duke of Touraine: 'He was also Duke of Touraine (1386–1392)'.
1392: Louis of Orleans' Touraine title ends ('Duke of Touraine (1386–1392)'); he is Duke of Orleans from 4 June 1392.
1417: the Dauphin Charles becomes Duke of Touraine and Count of Poitou: infobox 'Duke of Touraine Count of Poitou 1417 – 21 October 1422'.
21 October 1422: Charles succeeds as King Charles VII and the duchy is 'Merged in the crown'.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the extent is the gazetteer's Touraine (Indre-et-Loire), an approximation of the historical county and duchy.
